scores.evidence: CI commits the new tag to the config repo. Argo CD syncs it ... so CI holds no cluster credentials
scores.rationale: OIDC, cosign, admission pinning and GitOps pull are used correctly; minor issue that tag-based config commits are not explicitly digest-pinned and CI still has write access to the config repo.

scores.evidence: Brownfield (ASSUMED): the 50 services already ship through existing per-team pipelines.
scores.rationale: Covers migration, trust, capacity, and decommission credibly, but omits contract testing, flaky tests and DB migration compatibility as core needs.

scores.evidence: Exactly one deployer per service. ... Sync is one-way, with no dual deploy.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, flag-based ownership and phase dependencies are consistent; small loose ends such as config repo vs old pipeline as release history.

scores.evidence: unsigned image, image signed by another identity, image from a PR or fork, cross-service credential use, tampered digest
scores.rationale: Validation tied to specific risks, early (V0, V3 before prod), with shadow-run digest compare and post-launch SLIs; thresholds are labelled baseline or assumption.

scores.evidence: UNKNOWN: needs the availability engineering leadership commits to, before Phase 3
scores.rationale: Assumptions and unknowns are explicitly labelled, ranked, with triggers and what changes if wrong.

scores.evidence: Worst failure: A compromised or misconfigured pipeline deploys an unverified artifact to prod across many services at once.
scores.rationale: Covers compromise, outage/hotfix, double-deploy, break-glass and rollback; thin on flaky tests, schema migration failures and partial-failure retries.

scores.evidence: SLIs and burn-rate alerts against the SLO. Platform backup/restore and DR drill.
scores.rationale: Rollback, monitoring, DR drills and on-call are addressed, but owner and team size are unknown and delivery metrics are thin.

scores.evidence: Load-test runners at 2× peak and record the cost per build. Meter cost per team and service.
scores.rationale: Identifies cost measurement and controls and buy-vs-build, but gives no volume-based estimate and the budget is UNKNOWN.

scores.evidence: R3: trust boundary; prod admission and every service's credentials rest on it
scores.rationale: Explicit reversibility classes, validation and revisit triggers per decision, defined point of no return and exit paths.

scores.evidence: Adopt the org's existing or a managed CI engine and GitOps controller; build only the templates and policy layer
scores.rationale: Uses existing tools, defers portal, multi-region and per-PR environments with pull-forward triggers; sized sensibly.

scores.evidence: Wave 1: ~5 non-critical services. Wave 2: ~15 services. Wave 3: the rest, tier-1 last.
scores.rationale: Dependency-justified phases, concrete first slice, checkable exits and failure fallbacks per check.

checklist.evidence: Migrate one pilot per archetype (≥3), including one stateful or migration-heavy service ... Each keeps the old-pipeline fallback.
shadow-run builds against the old pipeline and compare image digests
OIDC-federated short-lived CI credentials (no long-lived secrets) ... image from a PR or fork
cosign-signed images with provenance and SBOM; admission policy ... pins the platform build identity
Ephemeral per-PR environments: Pulled forward if integration-test contention shows up
Load-test runners at 2× peak and record the cost per build.
SLIs and burn-rate alerts against the SLO.
an audit log of every deploy and approval.

traps.evidence: Service-by-service flag cutover (`use_new_pipeline`), old pipeline kept as fallback.
OIDC-federated short-lived CI credentials (no long-lived secrets)
